messages:
claire: quick FYI — PR #4329 preview is returning redirects -> 404s after the token rotation earlier. preview: https://deploy-preview-4329--docs.redwood.com

sam: ugh. saw a similar thing yesterday when NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN changed. can you paste the Netlify deploy log?

claire: copy-pasting the tail of the netlify log:
```
7:41:12 PM: Fetching site settings
7:41:18 PM: Redirect rules loaded from _redirects
7:41:18 PM: WARN failure applying redirect rules: 403 for private asset
7:41:19 PM: Build finished with warnings
7:41:19 PM: Published to draft URL
```

jordan: sounds like the preview deploy doesn't have the new token/role to fetch private assets (fonts/redirect-based assets). netlify previews still use the org-level token in our CI. when we rotated, the env var name changed in the infra config.

sam: right — our _infra repo renamed NETLIFY_PREVIEW_TOKEN -> NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN last week. the docs CI job still injects the old var. simple fix: update the docs preview step to use $NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN.

claire: i can push a tiny fix to the workflow, but wondering about backlog: merge now (hotfix) or wait for green preview? we also have other docs PRs queued.

michael: hold on merge. previews are our main safety net for redirects. if we merge without a clean preview we risk breaking prod redirects. can we speed up the preview so we don't block?

sam: two small ideas to speed iteration: 1) parallelize the docs-preview job so it doesn't wait on the full integ tests; 2) allow a manual "quick preview" job that only builds site without asset sync.

claire: both sound good. how invasive is 1)?

sam: we can flip the workflow to use matrix with `include: docs-quick` and `docs-full`. quick runs mkdocs build only. patch is ~6 lines in .github/workflows/docs.yml. example snippet: 
```
jobs:
  docs-preview:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        type: [quick, full]
    steps:
      - run: if [ "$${{ matrix.type }}" = "quick" ]; then mkdocs build; else mkdocs build && ./scripts/sync-assets.sh; fi
```

jordan: that's safe. quick preview won't publish to production artifacts, just the draft preview URL we use for review. it also avoids fetching private storage keys.

claire: in the meantime i'll push the env var rename + a note in the PR description about holding merge until preview is green. also adding local serve hints for reviewers who can't wait for netlify:
```
# local dev instructions
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs serve --dev-addr=127.0.0.1:8000
# if you need the redirect rules locally
python -m http.server 9000 --directory docs/site
```

michael: nice. add a short checklist in the PR template so folks know to check the redirect flow and fonts. i can review once the preview is green.

docs-bot: Netlify deploy queued for PR #4329 — draft preview URL will appear in CI once the build completes.

claire: thanks — i'll open the workflow PR and link it here. tagging reviewers @sam @michael for quick eyes. plan: patch workflow + env var fix, then rerun preview._hold merge until last green preview._ :thumbsup:

sam: thanks. if anyone hits the private asset 403 after this, try deleting the netlify cache in the deploy settings or bumping the preview cache key in the build (we add `PREVIEW_CACHE_KEY: $GITHUB_SHA` in the matrix quick run).

jordan: noted. filing a follow-up to update the docs contributor guide with the local redirect tip and the preview troubleshooting steps.

michael: will review the workflow PR later today. once green, let's do a staggered merge (docs quick merges first, then full).

claire: 👍 will post status updates in this thread when the PRs are open and when the preview is green.
